description: We are beaver FANATICS. We have the Beaver Fever and love python as well and fires, and El Nino, and burning.
summary: We developed a spatial dashboard that maps monthly vegetation health, beaver habitats, and wildfires across North America (excluding Mexico). Users can visually track how regions inhabited by beavers, nature’s ecosystem engineers, experience fewer wildfires and faster post-fire vegetation recovery.
details:
What does it do how does it work?:

A website that shows the monthly vegetation health index, areas of beavers, and wildfires across all of Canada, and the US. Users can observe how these element change in the map, and how regions with more beavers would observe less wildfires, and quicker recovery of the vegetation health in beavers inhabited areas. The time slider for the map would include the main wildfire months from April to October from the years 2015-2025. For 2026, we only include the months from April to September since NASA does not have the data for October 2026 yet.

- Alongside the adjustable map, we also include the statistics behind the correlation in a non technical manner, and why beavers behaviours lead to them being good wildfire mitigators.

What benefits does it have?

- This project aims to narrow the gap between science enthusiasm and science literacy. In a 2016 study by NASA, it is highlighted that while 51% of the participants are interested in science, only 28% have the literacy to read moderately sophisticated science news, and have the ability to engage in public policy debates.

- With wildfires being a prominent phenomena in the last 3 summers, we chose to highlight an important ecological buddy who have been helping us and their local wildlife counterparts over the course of the intense summers by providing a refuge when the fires are raging, and a better baseline for the vegetation and forest to recover after the burning.

What is the intended impact of the project?

- There are 2 main impacts of the project:

+) The first is to increase the scientific capability of people who are not or who do not feel like they are part of the science community from the angle of citizen science.

+) The second impact is to raise awareness on the role of beavers in the face of climate change. Many people only view them as a pest, whose sole purpose is to flood or damage their property. But beavers are an instrumental species in maintaining the health of their ecosystem due to their role as ecosystem engineers. By highlighting an observable and impressive effort that comes from beavers actions, we hope that people could realize the value of these fellow in a new lense.

-- Beyond beavers, we hope that this website skeleton can be extended to other animals too, like goats, sheeps, cattles, or the bison. For the first 3 animals, we have reviewed and recognize that governmental organizations are utilizing them to stamp out fuel sources before the fire season. So a skeleton framework website like this could be used to highlight those efforts to the public, so initiatives like these could get more funding and support. As for the bison, they are considered a threatened species, and most of them are no longer roaming the natural areas they used to. But there are some literature supporting the role of bison in wildfire prevention. They are a migratory species, so they consume and stamp out potential fuel sources in their habitat, however, most bisons are kept in confined areas nowadays so they do not migrate as far and wide as they used to. The Great Plains of North America are also suffering from wildfires, and bisons' migration used to cover most of this region. Perhaps a reintroduction of the bison here could not only help with their ecology, but also benefit humans living in the same area as well.

What tools did we use to develop our project?

- For our backend and data preprocessing, we relied on Python scripts. As for the frontend, we used React. The data that we used came from NASA in the form of NDVI, and monthly burned areas. We also got the shape of Canada and the US from the Canadian government (Statistics Canada), and the US boundary from the United States Census Bureau. For beavers data, GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility) provided us with sightings of these animals.

What factors did your team consider?

- The factors we considered are: Unique trend in climate change, general trend across North America, and scalability to other animals.

+) Unique Trend in climate change: To make our project unique in climate change trend, we aimed to highlight the role of beavers in wildfires. Wildfires have been a common sight and topic discussion for the past 3 years, and a lot of public news surrounding fighting wildfires only tackle human efforts in stamping out fires once they occur. So pivoting to wildfire prevention is a more unique and positive angle to consider.

+) General Trend: The literature we came across while doing this project are limited to local provinces or states. We aim to see if this is a general observable trend across both Canada and the US to reach a more generalized conclusion.

+) Scalability: While beavers have researches and an abundance of data to work with, we hope that we could further expand to other animals, especially ones that are threatened or endangered because it could also help with conservation status. If we could show that these animals help with wildfire mitigation, potentially, more funding and resources could be given to aid with conservation efforts for them.
